project: LNG plant turnaround — 4D BIM shutdown planning
client_owner: LNG operator (Woodside Energy provided data and in-kind support)
delivery: Curtin University research team with the operator
bim_tools: 4D BIM: laser scan to manually built 3D model of the compressor area, linked to the turnaround schedule. No modelling, scanning or 4D product is named; data sources were the operator's SAP and DRIMS
measured_benefit: 11.6 days actual against a 13.5-day adjusted plan and a 12-day target; 2.4 days saved in total (~17%); AUD 19M actual against an AUD 24.1M initial budget; 17 lift conflicts and 104 constructability issues caught pre-execution
evidence_basis: Peer-reviewed conference paper (ISARC 2018) with actuals from the operator's SAP and DRIMS systems, benchmarked against the previous equivalent turnaround
caveat: Single self-reported case, no control. The paper headlines AUD 4.1M saved while its own figures imply ~AUD 5.1M. Gains follow from re-sequencing, extra cranes and permit fixes that BIM enabled but did not solely cause.
